import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'is_fraud' to a categorical type with meaningful labels for better plotting
df['is_fraud_label'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'No Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set a visually appealing style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(20, 6))
fig.suptitle('Transaction Characteristics Analysis', fontsize=16)

# Plot 1: Transaction Counts by Type, colored by Fraud Status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[0], palette='viridis', order=df['transaction_type'].value_counts().index)
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Counts by Type and Fraud Status')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions')
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status')

# Plot 2: Transaction Counts by Hour of Day, colored by Fraud Status
# Ensure all hours are represented on the x-axis if possible, or sort them
sns.countplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud_label', ax=axes[1], palette='viridis', order=sorted(df['hour_of_day'].unique()))
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Counts by Hour of Day and Fraud Status')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions')
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status')
if len(df['hour_of_day'].unique()) > 10: # Adjust x-ticks for dense hourly data
    axes[1].set_xticks(range(0, 24, 2))
    axes[1].set_xticklabels(range(0, 24, 2))

# Plot 3: Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status
# Using violin plot to show distribution shape, median, and quartiles
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='is_fraud_label', y='amount', ax=axes[2], palette='viridis')
axes[2].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status')
axes[2].set_xlabel('Fraud Status')
axes[2].set_ylabel('Transaction Amount')

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the plot as output.png
plt.savefig('output.png')
